title: Other Reformed: grace works in the will itself
source_text: LIV. Verum alii Scholae Reformatae Theologi volunt immediatam gratiae operationem non solum mentem attingere, dum eam illuminat, & nova luce perfundit, sed ipsam quoque voluntatem, in qua consensum illum, quem divinis monitis adhibet, realiter & Physice operatur.
pass_a_gloss: LIV. But other Theologians of the Reformed School hold that the immediate operation of grace not only touches the mind, while it illuminates it, & floods it with new light, but also the will itself, in which it works really & Physically that consent, which it gives to the divine admonitions.
pass_b_english: Thesis LIV. Other theologians of the Reformed school, however, hold that grace acts directly not only on the mind, enlightening it and flooding it with new light, but on the will itself as well.
In the will, they say, grace really and physically produces the consent that the will gives to God's admonitions.

lemmas.latin: immediatam gratiae operationem non solum mentem attingere
lemmas.gloss: the immediate operation of grace not only touches the mind
and floods it with new light

choices.why: The term for grace working in the will itself as a cause, against working only through moral persuasion.
